Title: next.config.ts declares nextConfig twice; build and dev both crash

Recommended_Action: Delete the duplicate declaration; merge its redirects() (/life -> /life/places) into the single nextConfig
Acceptance_Criteria: next build exits 0 from clean clone; next dev boots; GET /life 308-redirects to /life/places; no change to headers

Title: No Content-Security-Policy header

Title: X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors intentionally omitted (preview-tool framing)

Recommended_Action: Add frame-ancestors with known preview origins (or X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN) once preview tooling identified
Acceptance_Criteria: Framing from unknown origin blocked; preview tool still works

Title: clientIp trusts leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry (spoofable behind Vercel)
Evidence: src/lib/ratelimit.ts lines 11-13 splits XFF and takes [0]; Vercel appends the real client IP so leftmost is attacker-controlled; weakens signup/report/login limits and anonymous actorKey (src/lib/actor.ts line 9)
Recommended_Action: Use the platform-trusted position (rightmost hop on Vercel or x-real-ip set by edge); verify with forged-header test on the real deployment
Acceptance_Criteria: Forged XFF no longer evades signup/report limits on production; actor dedupe holds under rotation attempts

Title: Rate limiter is in-memory per process
Evidence: src/lib/ratelimit.ts lines 5-7 (documented limitation); limits reset on cold start and are not shared across instances
Recommended_Action: Accept for MVP as documented risk; if abuse appears move counters to Postgres or Vercel KV keyed by IP/account
Acceptance_Criteria: Either documented accepted risk or persisted counters with verified enforcement in prod

Title: Alert dispatch loads all verified subscribers unbounded and updates one row per email
